messages:
Sam: Heads-up, I'm seeing a bunch of small GPU pods pending in eu-west-1 this morning. They request fractional GPUs (vGPU) and the autoscaler isn't bringing up the expected pool.
Nina: Which node pools do those pods target? mig or time-slice pools?
Sam: They should be schedulable on the 'shared-gpu' nodepool we launched with time-slicing and on the MIG-enabled 'mig-8g' pool. PodSpec uses tolerations for both.
Igor: autoscaler logs show it's preferring to spin up full 8-GPU nodes for mig-8g but our scheduler prefers packing vGPUs on timeslice nodes. Might be mismatch in resource requests vs allocatable.
Marta: Can you paste a sample PodSpec? We require the annotation for fractional vGPU right now.
Sam: Sure: 
```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: small-train
  annotations:
    redwood/gpu-mode: "timeslice"
spec:
  containers:
  - name: worker
    image: redwood/py:3.10
    resources:
      limits:
        nvidia.com/gpu: "0.25"
      requests:
        cpu: "1"
        memory: "4Gi"
    nodeSelector:
      gpu.redwood.com/type: shared-timeslice
```
Nina: That request (nvidia.com/gpu: "0.25") is fine for our scheduler plugin, but cluster-autoscaler needs thresholds to trigger creating time-slice nodes. Right now CA is configured with expander: least-waste which picks mig-8g because it thinks it'll reduce pending count faster.
Igor: We also have node-group balancing enabled. If mig-8g is already underutilized in us-east and eu-west has none, CA will try to avoid adding more diversity.
Marta: Cost question: spinning up full MIG nodes (8g) is ~3x the cost of a timeslice instance for same throughput when running many small jobs. We should bias autoscaler to prefer timeslice pool for fractional requests.
Sam: Proposal: add a node affinity rule at pod admission (via mutating webhook) to prefer shared-timeslice if cpu<=2 and gpu<1, and tweak CA expander to 'most-pods' for those node groups. Thoughts?
Igor: I like mutating webhook + taint-based fallback. e.g., taint timeslice-only: gpu-mode=timeslice:NoSchedule, then tolerate via annotation. That way pods explicitly opt-in. Also set CA 'scaleDownUnneededTime' shorter for timeslice pool to avoid long idle costs.
Nina: We should also ensure kubelet allocatable reflects fractional availability. Some nodes report allocatable as integer GPUs which blocks scheduling. Need to set device-plugin properly: the vGPU device-plugin reports fractional resources as extended resources (gpu.redwood.com/vgpu-0.25).
Marta: Another gotcha: MIG profiles on A100 require node labels like nvidia.com/mig.mode=enabled and pod annotation nvidia.com/mig.request. We have a mix of MIG and time-slice images; recommend three pools: timeslice-shared, mig-4g (for medium jobs), mig-8g (for large). Keep mig pools in limited regions.
autoscaler-bot: [info] Suggested scale action: add 3 nodes to nodegroup shared-timeslice-eu-west (type c6g.gpu.timeslice). Reason: 12 pending pods matching nodeSelector gpu.redwood.com/type=shared-timeslice.\Sam: Fine, but how to make CA prefer shared-timeslice? Can set nodeGroup config with 'priority': higher for shared-timeslice in custom CA wrapper, or use different instance types with lower estimated startup time.
Igor: We already have a CA wrapper (scale-manager) that can inject preferred nodegroups via a policy file. I'll add a rule: if average pending pods per nodegroup tag 'gpu-mode=timeslice' > 0.5 and pending pod gpu request <1, prefer shared-timeslice.
Nina: Also add monitoring alert: pending_gpu_pods_by_mode > 5 for 5m -> paging, and a daily cost report that shows per-mode $/GPU-hour so we can measure impact.
Marta: Agree. I'll add an eval job to run a synthetic 0.25 GPU workload and compare latency/cost across pools.
Sam: Quick action items: 1) Igor update scale-manager policy; 2) Nina verify device-plugin reports fractional allocatable; 3) Marta run eval; 4) Igor add taint+webhook PR. I'll follow up in ops board. :thumbsup:
Nina: I'll look at kubelet logs and device-plugin now, ping if you want me to drop any debug pods.
Igor: Creating PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/412 (policy + taint + CA tweak). ETA 2d.
Sam: Thanks — let's watch autoscaler metrics after merge and iterate.
